results.label: a regex stripper removes the newline that ASI needs: `return\n1` becomes `return1`, and the program stops doing what it did
a regex stripper cuts a string that contains `//` and the result is no longer a program
a regex stripper cuts a template that contains `/*`
a regex stripper turns a division followed by a regular expression into `//` and cuts the rest of the line
the tool handles all four of those cases: 4/4 behave identically after compression (the regex stripper: 0/4)
a blind renamer rewrites the name inside a string and the program prints something different
a blind renamer walks straight into `eval` and the value disappears (the name it builds at run time no longer exists)
a blind renamer changes `fn.name`, which other code can read
the tool leaves all three alone: the string, the eval file and the function name all behave identically (renaming is 0 in the eval and fn.name cases, and blocked by the word in the string)
a blind unused-variable remover deletes the call: "side effect happened" stops being logged
a blind unused-variable remover deletes a property read that advances a getter
the tool keeps the call and keeps the getter read, and says how many initialisers it kept as statements
the naive output has no map, so its stack frame can only be read against the minified text
the tool's output carries a map, and the frame resolves to the original line that actually threw
the application ships 85 readable JavaScript files, 2044343 bytes, 0 minified and 0 with a source map — the state before this tool is run
running the tool over that tree produces a number the tool is judged by: it prints the tree in fewer bytes and maps every position back

scope: the control: a regex stripper, a blind renamer and a blind unused-variable remover, each implemented here and each measured breaking a program that the tool handles correctly, plus the no-map baseline and the application tree's measurable state before the tool runs.
